name: conspicuous
definition: Easily seen; standing out at a glance. A conspicuous feature draws the eye first, but is often shared with look-alikes, so it rarely settles an identification on its own.
example: Field marks are listed conspicuous to diagnostic — the obvious first, the decisive last.

name: diagnostic
definition: Decisive for identification — the feature that separates a species from its closest relatives, even when it is subtle and easy to miss.
example: The orange band on the connexivum is diagnostic for the small milkweed bug.

name: field-mark
definition: A visible feature used to identify an organism in the field — a wing band, a spot, a body shape, a leg posture.

name: connexivum
definition: The exposed lateral rim of a true bug's abdomen, visible from above beyond the folded wings and often marked with alternating bands.

name: scutellum
definition: The triangular, shield-shaped plate on the back of a true bug or beetle, set between the bases of the wings.
example: A dark scutellum with white markings.

name: pronotum
definition: The plate covering the top of the first thoracic segment, just behind an insect's head.

name: dorsum
definition: The upper surface, or back, of an animal.
example: Bold white spots and streaks on the dorsum.

name: frons
definition: The front of an insect's head, between and below the compound eyes.
example: The bull's-eye frons mark of the common green darner.

name: venation
definition: The pattern of veins in an insect's wing — a key character for telling orders and families apart.

name: aposematic
definition: Describing warning coloration or signals that advertise an animal is toxic, distasteful, or dangerous to would-be predators.
example: The monarch's aposematic orange warns birds to leave it alone.

name: voltinism
definition: The number of generations, or broods, a species completes in a single year.

name: multivoltine
definition: Completing three or more generations per year.

name: elytra
definition: The hardened forewings of a beetle, which fold back as protective covers over the membranous hindwings.

name: cephalothorax
definition: The fused head-and-thorax body region of a spider or other arachnid, bearing the eyes, mouthparts, and legs.
example: The crab spider's small cephalothorax and globose abdomen.

name: instar
definition: A developmental stage of an insect between two successive moults.

name: nectaring
definition: Feeding on flower nectar, as an adult butterfly, bee, or other pollinator does.
example: The painted lady was nectaring on a zinnia in the afternoon sun.
